claims.text: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large caloric effect under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The as-fabricated alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking.
A continuous SiC coating approximately 1–5 μm thick should be deposited on the alloy by CVD.
The proposed SiC coating is stable at high temperature.
The SiC coating will suppress surface crack initiation.
The SiC coating will limit crack propagation.
SiC provides a high-hardness surface reinforcement.
The hardness and toughness of the SiC coating will reduce surface stress concentrations.
Arresting surface microcracks will improve the alloy's overall mechanical integrity and fracture resistance.
A thin surface coating will not interfere materially with the calorically active bulk alloy.
The coated material is expected to have compressive strength appreciably higher than 218 MPa.
The caloric response of the coated alloy is expected to remain within ±10% of that of the uncoated alloy.
The uncoated alloy has a baseline compressive-strength range of 152–218 MPa.
The intervention is intended to remain effective during applied-field and pressure-field cycling.
The intervention is intended to remain effective from room temperature to approximately 600 °C.
The intervention is intended to remain effective under compressive strain rates typical of caloric actuators.
The quantitative effects of coating on strength, caloric performance, and thermal transport remain to be experimentally verified.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field assigns the 152–218 MPa range from epoxy-composite routes to the uncoated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 baseline, whereas the baseline and initial-state fields identify the baseline as the unchanged alloy. The query attributes those values to epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, not to the unchanged target alloy.
